question_content: I finally decided to leave BT, but my new broadband provider, Wildanet, don't offer email, so I also signed up with Proton for email. I used Proton Bridge to manage the transition, which worked fine. The info from BT told me that their free "basic" email service does not work with clients (such as Thunderbird) and I would have always to log into the BT mail website to check, receive or send emails. I therefore resolved to move all my contacts to my new Proton address as soon as possible. I also opted to use the Proton import feature to import all my archive emails from the BT server. When I set up Thunderbird to access both my old BT email account and my new Proton account, I was surprised to see that my import had been unnecessary, as Thunderbird has actually fetched all my BT emails and continued to do so, despite BT having said it would not be able to. The only hiccup was that I now had two sets of local folders storing my saved emails - one from Thunderbird, and the other from the Proton import. The imported one's folder names were the same as the Thunderbird ones, but were all preceded by [INBOX}, such as [INBOX]Banking for example. Not needing two sets of saved email folders, when I had finished informing all my contacts to move to Proton, I set about rationalising my two sets of folders. I was part way through renaming the imported folders to get rid of the [INBOX} prefix, when Thunderbird stopped doing any more renaming, and also stopped receiving emails from either server. It did manage to send an outgoing email, but then reported that it could not save a copy to the sent folder because of "file permissions". It seems to me that something I have done during this folder clean up process has messed up Thunderbird's normal operation, but I don't know what exactly I did, or what I can do to recover from it. Any help would be appreciated. Dave Leonard

A re-test also fails, as does trying POP3.  But when I try to add one of my regular (charter.net ISP) email accounts it proceeds normally and finds the account.  When I try "get a new account" I get a window with the error message "sorry, we're unable to communicate with out sign up server".   So it's working with my Charter.net account but not with the gmail account.  I've checked proxy settings and changed to No Proxy but that didn't help.  I've triple checked my entries for my gmail address, and compared them exactly with my gmail profile.. What to do next...is it possible that this older version of Thunderbird has stored some obsolete gmail settings?  If so, can they be changed?
